title: Quantum Codes with Arbitrary Z-Rotation logical Gates and Applications to Fault-Tolerant Code Switching
authors: Reza Dastbasteh, Ruben M. Otxoa, Pedro M. Crespo, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez
abstract: A technique for realizing a universal set of fault-tolerant quantum operations is the code switching method, which leverages two quantum codes with complementary sets of transversal gates. To date, the application of this technique has been largely limited to families of color codes supporting a logical $T$ gate. No analogous code switching protocols exist for many other prominent families, such as rotated surface codes, or for finer $Z$-rotation gates. In this work, we first utilize the doubling technique as a unified framework to construct a class of quantum color codes encoding a single logical qubit with an arbitrarily large minimum distance, enabling the transversal realization of arbitrary small logical $Z$-rotation gates. We investigate the structural properties of this code family, demonstrating that they improve upon the parameters of state-of-the-art triorthogonal codes, achieve lower qubit overhead compared to certain known color codes, and admit single-shot decoding of $Z$-syndromes via meta-checks. Furthermore, we show that this framework extends beyond color codes; specifically, it enables the generation of $r$-orthogonal quantum codes, $r \ge 2$, that inherit the local geometry of rotated surface codes. We then provide an overhead optimization protocol alongside several candidate codes tailored for realizing logical $Z$-rotation gates within rotated surface codes. Finally, we extend the fault-tolerant code switching protocol based on transversal CNOT gates to incorporate fault-tolerant realization of $Z$-rotation gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy for geometries compatible with rotated surface codes. We present the first demonstration of fault-tolerant magic state preparation by means of code switching within a distance-three rotated surface code using a total footprint of only 45 physical qubits, and evaluate its performance through a simulation.
summary: This paper develops advanced techniques for constructing fault-tolerant quantum error correcting codes that support arbitrary Z-rotation logical gates. By extending the code switching protocol to new families of codes, such as those compatible with rotated surface codes, it significantly improves the theoretical feasibility and resource estimates for universal quantum computation beyond standard T-gate assumptions.
main_problem: The core problem is realizing a universal set of fault-tolerant quantum operations, specifically incorporating arbitrary Z-rotation logical gates (RZ(theta)), into existing quantum error correction frameworks.
main_result: The authors construct new classes of quantum color codes and $r$-orthogonal codes that support transversal RZ(theta) gates, extending the code switching protocol to these geometries.
method: They utilize the doubling technique as a unified framework for constructing these codes and extend the code-switching method by incorporating fault-tolerant Z-rotation gate realization into protocols designed for rotated surface codes.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum error correcting codes, including color codes and rotated surface codes. The goal is to encode logical qubits while maintaining high minimum distance ($d$) against noise.
key_observables: Minimum distance ($d$), qubit overhead (physical vs. logical), and the feasibility of fault-tolerant gate implementation (e.g., magic state preparation).
important_parameters: Arbitrarily large minimum distance, specific rotation angles $	ext{RZ}(	heta)$, and physical qubit counts (e.g., 45 qubits for a demonstration).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending protocols previously limited to T-gate supporting color codes; the construction methods assume certain weight divisibility conditions are met.
figures_summary: No specific figure summaries were extracted, but the notes mention circuit diagrams illustrating S|+> preparation via code-switching between different code types.
paper_structure: The paper develops theory by first establishing new color codes using a doubling technique to support RZ(theta) gates. It then generalizes this framework to $r$-orthogonal codes compatible with rotated surface codes, culminating in the extension of the fault-tolerant code switching protocol for these geometries.
why_interesting: This work directly advances the theoretical understanding of resource efficiency in quantum computation by providing pathways to implement non-Clifford gates (like arbitrary Z-rotations) using more general and potentially less resource-intensive coding schemes than previously established methods.
